summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a new speech-to-text model available via two APIs (real-time streaming and pre-recorded processing) with improved word-error-rate and latency over its predecessor Chirp 3, and integrated across Gboard, Chrome, Antigravity and the Gemini app.

mechanisms.reason: The model can delegate tasks to other Gemini models via function calls, extending tool-use chains rather than just transcribing.
mechanisms.quote: Function calling: The model can delegate complex tasks (such as image generation and file analysis) to other Gemini models via function calls.

practices.reason: Teams building voice interfaces get a concretely faster and more accurate transcription model with stated benchmark gains over the prior model.
practices.quote: As measured by Artificial Analysis, time to final transcription, for example, improves by 70%.

practices.reason: The model introduces two distinct new API surfaces that a team would need to integrate depending on streaming vs. pre-recorded use case.
practices.quote: The model is available across two separate APIs: Real-time streaming ... Pre-recorded audio processing: Transcribes recorded audio, meetings, call logs, and more with speaker attribution and word-level timestamps via the Interactions API using gemini-3.5-transcribe .

practices.reason: The model publishes third-party WER benchmarks (Artificial Analysis, FLEURS) that a team could use as a reference point for evaluating transcription quality, though the methodology is not fully specified.
practices.quote: On the FLEURS benchmark across a set of top languages and locales, the model delivers precise multilingual performance, improving over Chirp 3, and achieving a 5.50% WER in streaming mode and 5.04% WER in non-streaming use-cases.
